learningObjective: Keep raw text in place, skip non-alphanumeric endpoints one at a time, and move both pointers only after a case-insensitive match.

mechanismReview.pattern: Two pointers moving inward over filtered endpoint characters.
mechanismReview.recognitionCue: Use opposite-end pointers when equality must hold symmetrically after ignoring characters, case, or other endpoint noise.
mechanismReview.invariant: Before each loop iteration, every accepted alphanumeric pair outside [left,right] matches case-insensitively; discarded outside characters are non-alphanumeric and cannot affect the answer.
mechanismReview.stateModel: Keep only left and right indices into the original text; skip exactly one invalid endpoint per iteration, compare valid endpoints, and move both only after equality.
mechanismReview.visualRationale: The full raw character array preserves punctuation and spacing while stable L and R keys visibly move inward; range, branch reason, and direction labels make each boundary movement explicit.
rejectedAlternatives: Building a normalized copy and reversing it is concise but uses O(n) extra space and hides endpoint skipping.
A normalized-only array erases the punctuation branches executed by the supplied implementation.
A prose comparison list cannot show that only one pointer moves on each skip branch.
mechanismReview.transferLesson: When irrelevant data appears at either boundary, repair one endpoint at a time until both are comparable; only then apply the symmetric predicate and advance both.

mediumRationale: An original, problem-specific trace shows the actual input, changing state, safe transition, and result. The static first frame works without JavaScript; controls add step-by-step playback without replacing the proof with decoration.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected: automatic graph layout would hide the exact data values and state changes that this problem needs.
mediumComparison.svg: Rejected: the trace is a changing data state, so semantic HTML keeps values selectable, readable, and responsive.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Selected: each problem owns concrete frames rendered as arrays, maps, grids, trees, stacks, queues, intervals, pointers, bits, or tensor shapes.
mediumComparison.interaction: Selected as progressive enhancement: Play, Previous, Next, and step buttons reveal the same authored frames while static HTML remains complete.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected: the visual is an original synthesis of the supplied implementation and does not reuse source artwork.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected: prose alone would make the learner simulate the changing data structure in working memory.

deckReview.notes: No source slide deck is part of the supplied coding guide. The visual was designed from this problem's source implementation and worked trace.

sourceReview.notes: The supplied Coding_Questions_Phone_Guide.md is the curriculum source. The task, implementation sketch, and complexity statement are preserved; the trace frames are original explanatory artwork.

agentReview.summary: Checked each authored frame against the implementation path, verified that the displayed state changes are problem-specific, and checked the static and interactive accessibility paths.

implementation.accessibility: The figure has a labelled title, a complete group description, visible values and state labels, a direct Read it this way caption, keyboard controls, and a static first-frame fallback.
